To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
motor learning principles can be used to design more effective rehabilitation techniques.
Motor learning is the acquisition of new motor skills through practice.

(i) Motor learning is an important component of recovery from brain injury; (ii) Patients with hemiparesi have deficits in motor learning; (iii) Recovery is a form of learning; and (iv) Motor learning principles should be incorporated in rehabilitation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a better understanding of the neural mechanisms of motor control and motor learning, and the translation of this knowledge to the clinical setting.
the development and testing of rehabilitation approaches that are based on motor learning theories.
how we can improve motor function after stroke by combining motor learning principles with new rehabilitation approaches.

motor learning is a useful concept in the context of neurorehabilitative research and clinical practice.
motor learning is a key component of both recovery and rehabilitation.
rehabilitation is a process that involves motor learning and motor learning is the basis for rehabilitation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
motor learning is relevant to neurorehabilitation and that rehabilitation approaches that are based on theories about motor learning have a promising future.

motor control approaches can provide a framework to address these questions.
